## Mountain weather

The Conditions tab now opens with an estimate of the weather where you are and on the highest ground nearby: temperature with a likely range, rain or snow, the snow level, the freezing level, and wind with gusts. A table steps up the mountain so you can see where rain turns to snow.

It is built from the National Weather Service forecast grid, nearby weather stations and SNOTEL in the US, and from Environment and Climate Change Canada's high-resolution forecast and stations in Canada, together with recent trail reports and the shape of the terrain. It is a model estimate, not an observation, and the card says so. Official forecasts and alerts stay right below it. You can turn it off in Settings.

## Fixes and hardening

- **Route privacy.** Shared route cards, GPX files and history exports now leave out every point within the privacy distance (about 650 ft by default) of the start and the end, measured in a straight line, as well as that distance along the path. Before, a trip that circled the block or doubled back past the driveway could still show a point right at home.
- **Backups on Android.** Saving a backup over an older, larger file could leave the old bytes at the end and make the zip unreadable. Backups and exports now replace the file completely.
- **Recorded trips.** If Android stopped the app in the middle of writing a point, every point after it was dropped when the trip was read back. A damaged line is now skipped on its own, and new points start on a fresh line. Trip summaries and region lists are written so a crash cannot leave them half saved.
- **Recording recovery.** When Android restarts a recording, it now keeps the pause state and the step count instead of resetting them.
- **Offline regions.** Deleting a region while it was still downloading no longer brings it back when the download ends.
- **Restore.** A damaged or oversized backup can no longer fill the phone or crash the app; each file is checked and written under a temporary name first.
- **Network cache.** A failed write can no longer pair an old cached copy with a new timestamp, and unusually large responses are refused instead of read into memory.
- **Page security.** The map page now carries a Content Security Policy: only the app's own bundled scripts run, and no frames load. On iOS, only the app's own page can call native code, and the offline proxy refuses requests it cannot cache correctly.
